clue.text: Work out in column, say, exercising butt also

definitions.note: a verb: to total part of a column of figures

indicators.note: exercising puts the words through their paces, working them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fitness tip: work out in a gym column while exercising your backside too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' suggests the gym; here it means calculating. 'exercising' rearranges BUTT ALSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding up a portion of a column of figures, before the grand total, is computing a partial sum.

clue.text: African country rejecting a new place for lions? That's unexpected

indicators.note: rejecting means the country throws out the following letters from its name

parts.note: Sudan is a country in north-east Africa
a den is a lair, such as a lions' den

explanation.surface: An African state turns down a new site for a lion enclosure, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' leaves SUD, which the parse cannot show; 'That's' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrupt and without warning is unforeseen: a synonym.

clue.text: Gracious Motown singer, a phenomenal youngster?

parts.note: the exclamations 'Gracious!' and 'Boy!' both express surprise
Stevie Wonder is a singer on the Motown label

explanation.surface: A tribute to a charming Motown star who was a child prodigy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gracious' reads as an adjective praising the singer; it is the exclamation of surprise. Robin, Batman's sidekick, is also known by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gifted child or prodigy is commonly called by this phrase, a fixed idiom.

clue.text: Actor in musical touring island

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the musical goes round the island letter

parts.note: Oliver! is the Lionel Bart musical

explanation.surface: A performer appears in a musical production that is on tour around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated English stage and screen performer.

clue.text: Some mash enhancing pasty

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook's tip: a bit of mash improves a pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like the Cornish pie but is the adjective meaning pale. A pasty is a pastry turnover with a savoury filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a pale, unhealthy-looking complexion: synonyms.

clue.text: Put an end to drink

definitions.meaning: to stamp out or quash a rumour or plan

explanation.definitionFit: One sense means to quash something; the other is the whisky distilled in Scotland.

clue.text: Indication of something missing when taking in a second-rate film

indicators.note: taking in means the mark holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: a caret is the proofreader's mark showing where something is to be inserted
B is the grade below A, so second-rate

explanation.surface: A critic complains that something is lacking when watching a mediocre movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1972 Bob Fosse musical set in Berlin is a well-known movie of this title.

clue.text: Silly person lifting prize-money without hesitation? About right

indicators.note: About means the reversed letters go around the following letter
lifting in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
without means the hesitation is removed from the word

parts.note: pewter is a slang term for prize money, after pewter trophies
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A fool pockets the winnings without a moment's pause, which seems about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' leaves PEWT; 'lifting' (upward in a down clue) gives TWEP, which 'About' wraps round the R. Prize-money is called pewter after pewter trophies.
explanation.definitionFit: A twit or idiot: an informal synonym for a foolish person.

clue.text: Rick's content to be with first woman in French play

parts.note: a rick is a stack of hay

indicators.note: in places the first woman inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A haystack's contents are placed beside the first woman in a French drama.
explanation.walkthrough: A rick is a farm stack of hay or straw.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward's 1925 comedy about the eccentric Bliss family bears this title.

clue.text: Journey terribly disheartened companion making set of panels

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: disheartened means the word loses its heart, keeping only its outside letters

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A journey leaves someone's travelling companion utterly dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' strips TERRIBLY to its ends, TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A triptych is a painting or carving on three hinged boards, often an altarpiece.

clue.text: It's helpful to see job revealing blatant overcharging

parts.note: daylight lets you see
a job is slang for a crime, such as a robbery

explanation.surface: A recruit finds that a clearer view of the job reveals a rip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'job' looks like employment; it is criminal slang for a heist.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being charged a scandalously excessive price, done openly.

clue.text: Film about, say, Paisley student in establishment?

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film
on means about, concerning
Ian Paisley was the Northern Irish politician, so Ian is an example of a Paisley

explanation.surface: A film concerning, for instance, Ian Paisley as a student in some institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'establishment' hints at Eton College, an elite English boarding school whose pupils are the Establishment's backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil at Eton College, a school of the British Establishment, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Government money in the US gets restricted support? That's not true

definitions.note: a fib: the definition names a lie, a noun

parts.note: pork is American slang for government money spent to win local votes

indicators.note: restricted means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: American pork-barrel money ends up as limited funding for some project, which the speaker calls false.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang: a 'pork pie' (porky) is a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang for a lie, a statement that is false.

clue.text: Woman wasted years? That's quite possible

parts.note: Ida is a woman's name

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so the word is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a woman's years have been squandered, and a listener cautiously agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase of cautious agreement meaning probably so or perhaps.

clue.text: Instant record showing game's highly fashionable

parts.note: snap is a children's card game; with 's it is snap's
hot means very much in vogue

explanation.surface: A record set instantly shows that a game has become very trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick photograph taken on the spur of the moment captures a single moment.

clue.text: Scrabble includes this gripping tense championship

indicators.note: gripping means holding, so the letter is placed inside

parts.note: Scrabble is played with letter tiles
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tense, gripping Scrabble final decides the championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning a championship means holding a sporting crown, such as a world boxing belt.

clue.text: Note time taken by son being cautious

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: taken by means the letter is held inside the following word

parts.note: a son of a place, such as a son of the soil, is one born there

explanation.surface: A note is taken away by a son who is being careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'son' means someone born in a place, as in 'a son of Yorkshire'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitant and unsure, proceeding with care rather than boldly.

clue.text: Character beginning to inspect reverse of, say, grey jacket

parts.note: a card is an eccentric, an amusing character

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of the next word is used
reverse of means the letters of the horse are read backwards

parts.note: a grey is a horse, and nag is a word for a horse; say marks the example

explanation.surface: A character starts checking the back of a grey jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grey' is a horse here, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted woollen top that buttons down the front, named after the Earl of Cardigan.

clue.text: A danger leaving back of house in showery period?

indicators.note: leaving means the letter departs from the word

parts.note: peril means danger

indicators.note: back of means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A danger: leaving the back of the house open during a rainy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes E, the last letter of 'house', out of PERIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month of the year is proverbially known for its showers.

clue.text: Gander's promiscuous, grabbing duck's tail and goose's

indicators.note: grabbing means holding, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: loose means sexually promiscuous

indicators.note: tail means the final letter of the bird's name is taken

parts.note: goose's tail, the last letter of goose

explanation.surface: A male goose is a philanderer, seizing a duck by the tail as well as a goose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' looks like the bird but is slang for a look; 'tail' carries over to the goose as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a gander means having a quick look, a slang synonym.

clue.text: Follower violating hard tenet largely

indicators.note: violating means abusing, so the letters are broken and rearranged
largely means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A disciple who breaks a strict principle, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts TENET to TENE; 'violating' shuffles HARD TENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter or disciple of a cause or creed is one who sticks to it.

clue.text: Carpet covering area above odd platform

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the first part over the second
covering means hiding, so the area letter is lost from sight

parts.note: to carpet is to reprimand, as is to roast
rum means strange or odd

explanation.surface: A carpet laid over an area sits above an unusual stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' looks like a rug; it is a verb meaning scold. 'covering' hides the A in ROAST, leaving ROST.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stand for a speaker or conductor is a dais or podium.

clue.text: There's a bit in such that concerns woman in union, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: bridal describes something relating to a bride, a woman being married

explanation.surface: A wedding speech reports something about a woman's marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' is the horse's mouthpiece, held in place by the headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's headgear holds the metal mouthpiece used to control it.

clue.text: Call promises to pay suspect

parts.note: to dub is to call or name
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A demand for payment on IOUs looks shady.
explanation.definitionFit: Questionable or doubtful, as an untrustworthy claim is.

clue.text: Crow showing feathers close to nest

parts.note: boas are feather stoles

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A crow displays its plumage near its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird; it is the verb meaning brag.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag or gloat about one's success.

clue.text: Revolutionary free to go round part of church in gloom

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning around, so the whole is read backwards
go round means the word encloses the next part

parts.note: to rid is to free
the apse is the semicircular end of a church

explanation.surface: A revolutionary is released to wander round part of a church in a dark mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round' gives RAPSEID, which 'Revolutionary' turns round; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep hopelessness and dejection, a state of darkness of spirit.

clue.text: Storehouse? It could be found with dash round place in Strasbourg

indicators.note: round means the first part goes around the second

parts.words: It could be found with dash
parts.note: in Morse code a dot is found alongside dashes
the European Parliament, EP, sits in Strasbourg

explanation.surface: A warehouse can be found with a dash round a place in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: A warehouse or storage facility where goods are kept.

clue.text: Sing with care around actor? One shows little concentration

indicators.note: around means the joined words wrap around the actor

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing, as is to grass
to mind is to care
Dennis Hopper was an American actor

explanation.surface: A singer takes care around an actor, who seems to be unfocused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sing' means inform to the police, British slang 'grass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flitting from topic to topic has an attention span likened to a jumping insect: idiom.

clue.text: Nationalist state, one that's unbalanced

parts.note: to utter is to state

explanation.surface: A nationalist's declaration reveals someone unstable.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a crazy person, someone mentally unbalanced.

clue.text: Team sped off in rush

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A team hurried away in a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlong rush, as of a panicked herd or crowd.
